name: @alessai/mybrowser-mcp

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL. Without tabId it uses this session's current tab, or opens a new temporary tab for the session if it has none.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (from new_tab or select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: browser_go_back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (from new_tab or select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: browser_go_forward
tools.description: Go forward to the next page

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (from new_tab or select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Let the page settle: waits up to `time` seconds and, for waits of 10 s or less, returns as soon as the page has been quiet for 1 s (exact:true sleeps the full time). To wait for something specific use browser_wait_for, which returns the moment it appears.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (from new_tab or select_tab), never the user's active tab.

time.description: Seconds to wait (required). Up to 10 s, returns early once the page has been quiet for 1 s; e.g. {time: 3}.

exact.description: Sleep the full time even if the page settles earlier (e.g. waiting for a timer).

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element. Target it by ref (e42 from a snapshot, o12 from browser_outline), mark, selector, role/name, matchText or label, or just describe it: {element: 'Publish button'}. Optional expect checks the result in the same call. E.g. {ref: 'o12'} or {element: 'Save', expect: 'Saved'}.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

element.description: What the element is, in plain words (e.g. 'Publish button'). With no ref/selector/role/name/matchText/label it is also the target: found on the page by code, site memory, then the decision model.

ref.description: Exact element reference: e42 from a snapshot, or o12 from browser_outline

mark.description: Set-of-Marks annotation number from annotated screenshot

selector.description: CSS selector to target the element directly

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. button, searchbox, link)

matchText.description: Visible text content to match on the element

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame.

expect.description: What should be true after the action, e.g. 'the Saved toast is shown'. The result then says confirmed, contradicted or not confirmed (checked for up to 3 s). Without a decision model only exact text is checked.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into an editable element (submit:true presses Enter). Target it like browser_click: ref, selector, role/name, label, or just {element: 'Email field'}. E.g. {ref: 'o7', text: 'hello'}. For several fields use browser_fill_form.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

element.description: What the element is, in plain words (e.g. 'Publish button'). With no ref/selector/role/name/matchText/label it is also the target: found on the page by code, site memory, then the decision model.

ref.description: Exact element reference: e42 from a snapshot, or o12 from browser_outline

mark.description: Set-of-Marks annotation number from annotated screenshot

selector.description: CSS selector to target the element directly

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. button, searchbox, link)

matchText.description: Visible text content to match on the element

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame.

expect.description: What should be true after the action, e.g. 'the Saved toast is shown'. The result then says confirmed, contradicted or not confirmed (checked for up to 3 s). Without a decision model only exact text is checked.

text.description: Text to type into the element

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Hover over an element. Target it like browser_click: ref, selector, role/name, matchText, label, or just {element: 'Account menu'}.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

element.description: What the element is, in plain words (e.g. 'Publish button'). With no ref/selector/role/name/matchText/label it is also the target: found on the page by code, site memory, then the decision model.

ref.description: Exact element reference: e42 from a snapshot, or o12 from browser_outline

mark.description: Set-of-Marks annotation number from annotated screenshot

selector.description: CSS selector to target the element directly

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. button, searchbox, link)

matchText.description: Visible text content to match on the element

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame.

expect.description: What should be true after the action, e.g. 'the Saved toast is shown'. The result then says confirmed, contradicted or not confirmed (checked for up to 3 s). Without a decision model only exact text is checked.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a key on the keyboard

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Perform drag and drop between two elements. Target by ref, mark number, or description.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

startRef.description: Exact source element reference from the page snapshot

startSelector.description: CSS selector for the source element

endRef.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

endSelector.description: CSS selector for the target element

tools.name: browser_mouse
tools.description: Click, double-click, right-click, hover, drag or scroll at a point of the last browser_screenshot, optionally typing text afterwards. For things with no element to target: canvases, slide or drawing editors, maps, and frames from other sites (e.g. PowerPoint/Word for the web). Take browser_screenshot of the tab first and give x/y in that image's pixels; a new screenshot is needed after the window is resized. Prefer browser_click and browser_type whenever the target appears in a snapshot.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

x.description: X in pixels of the last browser_screenshot of this tab (not page or screen pixels).

y.description: Y in pixels of the last browser_screenshot of this tab.

toX.description: drag only: end X in screenshot pixels.

toY.description: drag only: end Y in screenshot pixels.

deltaY.description: scroll only: vertical page pixels (positive scrolls down).

text.description: Typed with the keyboard after the action, into whatever then has focus.

tools.name: browser_select_option
tools.description: Select option(s) in a native dropdown. Target it like browser_click: ref, selector, role/name, label, or just {element: 'Country'}. E.g. {ref: 'o9', values: ['Oman']}. For several fields use browser_fill_form.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

element.description: What the element is, in plain words (e.g. 'Publish button'). With no ref/selector/role/name/matchText/label it is also the target: found on the page by code, site memory, then the decision model.

ref.description: Exact element reference: e42 from a snapshot, or o12 from browser_outline

mark.description: Set-of-Marks annotation number from annotated screenshot

selector.description: CSS selector to target the element directly

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. button, searchbox, link)

matchText.description: Visible text content to match on the element

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame.

expect.description: What should be true after the action, e.g. 'the Saved toast is shown'. The result then says confirmed, contradicted or not confirmed (checked for up to 3 s). Without a decision model only exact text is checked.

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page. Returns ARIA tree with element references for interaction. Default: viewport-only + auto diff (compact output on repeat calls). Pass mode:'full' to force the whole tree.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

viewportOnly.description: If true (default), only include elements visible in the viewport. Much smaller output. Set false for full page tree.

mode.description: 'full' returns the whole ARIA tree (original behavior). 'diff' returns only nodes added/removed/changed since the previous snapshot (requires a previous snapshot on the same tab + same viewportOnly setting + same URL). 'auto' (default) prefers diff when a usable baseline exists and the diff is meaningfully smaller; falls back to full otherwise. Diff saves tokens on multi-step flows where most of the page stays the same between calls.

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. By default, annotates interactive elements with numbered markers. Use the marker numbers with browser_click({mark: N}) to interact. If this fails with a chrome-extension access error, close DevTools and retry with conflicting extensions disabled.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

annotate.description: If true (default), overlay numbered markers on interactive elements and include a compact label map. Use mark numbers to click elements.

tools.name: browser_get_console_logs
tools.description: Get captured console logs. The first call starts capture for the tab and may return an empty list; call again after the behavior under test.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: browser_set_viewport
tools.description: Set browser viewport/device emulation for responsive testing using current primary presets: iphone, ipad, or desktop. Use browser_reset_viewport when finished.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

preset.description: Viewport preset to apply: iphone=402x874 DPR3, ipad=820x1180 DPR2, desktop=1920x1080 DPR1.

orientation.description: Optional orientation. Defaults to portrait for iphone/ipad and landscape for desktop.

tools.name: browser_reset_viewport
tools.description: Reset viewport/device emulation on the target tab back to the real browser window.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: browser_viewport_info
tools.description: Inspect the current viewport, window size, device pixel ratio, and any MyBrowser viewport preset applied to the target tab.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List all open browser tabs with their IDs, titles, URLs, and active status

tools.name: select_tab
tools.description: Make a tab this session's current tab, so tools without tabId act on it. The tab becomes this session's; a tab another agent session is using is refused.

tabId.description: The tab ID to switch to

tools.name: new_tab
tools.description: Opens a temporary tab by default. Call keep_tab to preserve it. Finish browser research with browser_cleanup.

url.description: URL to open in the new tab. Opens blank tab if omitted.

temporary.description: Temporary by default. Set false to preserve the tab without calling keep_tab.

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Close a specific browser tab by its ID

tabId.description: The tab ID to close

tools.name: keep_tab
tools.description: Preserve one tab created by this MCP session so browser_cleanup or session closure will not close it.

tabId.description: The temporary tab ID to preserve

browserId.description: Browser containing the tab. Defaults to this session's resolved browser.

tools.name: browser_cleanup
tools.description: Close every temporary tab this MCP session opened across connected browsers and return routing to the shared default. Call once after browser research, including failure paths.

tools.name: browser_extract
tools.description: Extract structured data from the page. Returns a JSON array of objects matching the field selectors. Treats the page as a data source — no snapshot or refs needed.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

selector.description: CSS selector for container elements to extract from (e.g. '.product-card', 'table tr')

fields.description: Map of field names to CSS selectors relative to each container. Use 'self' for the container's own text content, '@href' or '@src' for attribute values. Example: {"name": "h2 a", "price": ".price", "url": "a@href"}

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Find elements on the page by role, name, text, or selector, or by meaning with query (whole page, returns o-refs). Read-only — does not interact with elements.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

role.description: ARIA role to search for (e.g. button, link, searchbox)

name.description: Accessible name or partial text match

query.description: Find by meaning across the whole page, e.g. 'where do I set the end date'. Returns outline refs (o12) usable as ref in other tools.

tools.name: browser_fill_form
tools.description: Fill a form. Preferred: items, a list of {target, value} that is resolved against the whole page (sections, rows and below-the-fold included), set, and verified per item in one call, with dryRun to preview. Legacy: fields, a map of label to value for the visible form, with optional submit.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

fields.description: Map of field labels to values. Example: {"Username": "admin", "Password": "secret", "Country": "UAE"}

items.description: Set many controls in one call, anywhere on the page (below the fold included): text fields, checkboxes, switches, radios, native and custom dropdowns. Each is checked afterwards. Buttons and links are never clicked.

target.description: The control in plain words ('Daily budget', 'Threads placements') or an outline ref (o12)

value.description: Text to type, on/off for checkboxes and switches, or the option to choose

dryRun.description: With items: report which control each item maps to and what would change, without changing anything

submitAfter.description: Click the submit button after filling all fields

submitText.description: Text of submit button to click. Default: auto-detect (Submit, Login, Sign In, Save, Continue)

tools.name: browser_action
tools.description: Execute a sequence of browser actions in a single call. Combines click, type, navigate, wait, press_key, snapshot, screenshot, select_option, scroll, extract, and assert steps. Each step auto-waits for stable DOM after mutating actions. Returns per-step results with timing. Stops on first error by default. Use this to perform multi-step workflows efficiently in one round trip.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

ref.description: Element reference: e42 from a snapshot or o12 from browser_outline

text.description: Visible text to match (to find the element). For a type step with ref/selector/label given, text is the text to type.

key.description: Key name for press_key (e.g. Enter, ArrowDown)

time.description: Seconds to wait (for wait action). Up to 10 s it returns once the page is quiet unless exact is true.

exact.description: wait: sleep the full time even if the page settles earlier

condition.description: Condition for wait_for, same as browser_wait_for: text_visible, text_not_visible, url_contains, url_matches, element_visible, element_not_visible, network_idle. Put the text/URL in value and the CSS in selector, or write it as 'text_visible:Saved'.

value.description: wait_for: the text or URL part to wait for
Value to check against (URL substring, regex, text, etc.)

selector.description: CSS selector for element visibility checks

steps.description: Array of action steps to execute in sequence. Each step runs one browser action. The sequence stops on the first error by default. Supported actions: click, type, navigate, wait, wait_for, press_key, snapshot, screenshot, select_option, scroll, extract, assert.

stopOnError.description: Stop execution on first error (default true). Set false to continue through failures.

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until something is true, returning the moment it is. Code conditions: {condition: 'text_visible', value: 'Saved'} (also text_not_visible, url_contains, url_matches, network_idle) or {condition: 'element_visible', selector: '.done'} (also element_not_visible); shorthand {text: 'Saved'} works too. Or until: a plain-language state, e.g. {until: 'the upload has finished processing', failIf: 'an error is shown', timeout: 120000}, judged by the decision model every poll. timeout is in ms (default 10000). Use this instead of fixed waits and repeated snapshots.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

condition.description: Code check: url_contains, url_matches, element_visible, element_not_visible, text_visible, text_not_visible or network_idle. Omit when using until.

until.description: Plain-language state to wait for, e.g. 'the video upload has finished processing'. Needs a decision model; without one, use condition.

failIf.description: With until: stop early when this is true, e.g. 'an upload error is shown'

value.description: Parameter for the condition (URL substring, regex pattern, or text to match)

selector.description: CSS selector for element_visible / element_not_visible conditions

timeout.description: Max wait time in ms (default 10000; up to 300000 with until)

time.description: Seconds to simply wait when there is nothing specific to wait for (same as browser_wait).

tools.name: browser_assert
tools.description: Run many checks on the current page in one call. Returns pass/fail per check and does not throw. Check types: url_contains, url_matches, element_visible, element_not_visible, text_contains, text_not_contains, element_count, console_no_errors, title_contains, setting (a control's state or value: {type:'setting', target:'Advantage+ audience', expect:'off'}; the whole page is read, including below the fold, and the state is read by code), page (a yes/no question about the page; needs a decision model, otherwise returns needs_judgment with page text). Use setting checks instead of scrolling and snapshotting to verify forms and settings.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

target.description: setting: the control in plain words or an outline ref (o12), e.g. 'Advantage+ audience'

expect.description: setting: on, off, empty, or the value/option it should show. page: 'true' (default) or 'false'

match.description: setting: how values are compared (default exact, case-insensitive)

question.description: page: a yes/no question about the page, e.g. 'Is a sign-in wall shown?'

value.description: Value to check against (URL substring, regex, text, or title text)

checks.description: List of assertion checks to run

tools.name: browser_record_start
tools.description: Start recording browser actions. All subsequent browser tool calls will be captured as replayable steps until recording is stopped.

tabId.description: Tab where recording starts

tools.name: browser_record_stop
tools.description: Stop the current recording session. Returns the recorded steps and reports whether server persistence completed.

tools.name: browser_record_list
tools.description: List all saved recordings from both extension storage and server filesystem.

tools.name: browser_replay
tools.description: Replay a previously recorded browser session on one authorized tab. Supports runtime variables, speed control, and step ranges.

name.description: Name of the recording to replay

tabId.description: Authorized tab where the recording will replay

speed.description: Replay speed multiplier. 0 = fastest, 1 = original timing, 2 = 2x speed

startFromStep.description: Start replay from this step number (1-based, for debugging)

stopAtStep.description: Stop replay at this step number (for time-travel debugging)

tools.name: browser_learn
tools.description: Learn the current page's interactive elements and save a Page Object Model. Captures all interactive elements with stable CSS selectors. Results are persisted to ~/.mybrowser/sites/{domain}.json for future reference.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

pageName.description: Name for this page model (e.g. 'homepage', 'search', 'login'). If omitted, derived from page title.

tools.name: browser_site_info
tools.description: Return stored site knowledge for a domain, including known pages, element maps, flows, and quirks. Uses previously learned Page Object Models from browser_learn.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

domain.description: Domain to look up (e.g. 'github.com'). If omitted, uses the current tab's domain.

tools.name: list_browsers
tools.description: List connected browsers. Let normal calls use the shared default; call select_browser only when the user explicitly requests another browser.

tools.name: select_browser
tools.description: Use another browser for this session (by ID or name). Only when the user explicitly asked for a non-default browser. The choice sticks: do not call it before every action. It lasts until use_default_browser, browser_cleanup, the session ends, or 30 minutes without tool calls.

browserId.description: The browser to use: its ID (e.g. 'b1') or its name (e.g. 'MainLinux'). See list_browsers.

tools.name: use_default_browser
tools.description: Clear this session's browser override and return routing to the shared default browser.

tools.name: set_default_browser
tools.description: Save a shared default browser by stable browser name. Use this when multiple browsers are connected and you want future tool calls to prefer one browser unless a session-specific select_browser override is set.

browserId.description: The currently connected browser ID to save as the shared default. The browser's name is persisted, not the ephemeral ID.

tools.name: get_default_browser
tools.description: Show the shared default browser preference and whether it currently resolves to a connected browser.

tools.name: clear_default_browser
tools.description: Clear the shared default browser preference. After clearing, routing falls back to a session selection or auto-selects only when exactly one browser is connected.

tools.name: browser_claim_tab
tools.description: Claim exclusive ownership of a browser tab. Other sessions will not be able to perform mutating actions on this tab until it is released. Only needed in multi-session setups.

tabId.description: The tab ID to claim ownership of

browserId.description: Browser ID (from list_browsers). Defaults to active browser.

tools.name: browser_release_tab
tools.description: Release ownership of a browser tab so other sessions can claim or use it.

tabId.description: The tab ID to release ownership of

browserId.description: Browser ID. Defaults to active browser.

tools.name: browser_sessions
tools.description: List all active MCP sessions, their owned tabs, and target browser. Useful for understanding who is working on what in a multi-agent setup.

tools.name: browser_handoff
tools.description: Transfer ownership of a tab to another session. The current session must own the tab. Use browser_sessions to discover session IDs.

tabId.description: The tab ID to hand off

browserId.description: Browser ID. Defaults to active browser.

toSession.description: Target session ID or name to transfer ownership to

message.description: Optional message to accompany the handoff

tools.name: browser_shared_get
tools.description: Read a value from the shared inter-session key-value store.

key.description: The key to read from shared state

tools.name: browser_shared_set
tools.description: Write a value to the shared inter-session key-value store. Other sessions can read it with browser_shared_get.

key.description: The key to write to shared state

value.description: The value to store (any JSON-serializable value)

tools.name: browser_shared_delete
tools.description: Delete a key from the shared inter-session key-value store.

key.description: The key to delete from shared state

tools.name: browser_shared_list
tools.description: List all keys in the shared inter-session key-value store with their types and value previews.

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page (CDP Runtime.evaluate) and return the value of the last expression; promises are awaited. Read-only helpers are available as mb: mb.text(sel?), mb.texts(sel), mb.rows(tableSel?) -> [[cell...]], mb.links(sel?), mb.attr(sel, name), mb.count(sel), mb.visible(sel), mb.q/qa(sel), mb.waitFor(selectorOrTextOrFn, ms?) and mb.sleep(ms). Use one call for a whole loop (e.g. read every page of a list) instead of one call per step. To click or type, use the tools so targets are checked. E.g. {code: "mb.rows('table.results')"}.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

code.description: JavaScript to run in the page (required). The value of the last expression is returned; promises are awaited. E.g. "document.title" or "mb.rows('table')".

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds (default 5000; 15000 when the code uses mb.waitFor or mb.sleep)

frame.description: Work inside an embedded frame instead of the page: part of the frame's URL (e.g. "officeapps.live.com"). An unknown value lists the page's frames. Refs from a frame's snapshot only work with the same frame. Inside a frame the code runs as a page script, so pages that forbid eval refuse it.

tools.name: browser_storage
tools.description: Inspect and modify browser storage: localStorage, sessionStorage, and cookies. Use action 'get' to read, 'set' to write, 'delete' to remove a key, and 'clear' to remove entries. WARNING: clearing cookies WITHOUT a domain deletes ALL browser cookies and logs the user out of every website — that global wipe is refused unless confirmWipeAllCookies: true is set. Prefer passing domain to clear a single site's cookies.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

key.description: Storage key (required for get/set/delete on localStorage/sessionStorage)

value.description: Value to set (required for 'set' action on localStorage/sessionStorage)

domain.description: Cookie domain filter (only used with cookies type; scopes 'clear' to that site's cookies)

confirmWipeAllCookies.description: Required true to clear ALL browser cookies when no domain is given; wipes every website login

tools.name: browser_network
tools.description: Capture and inspect network requests. Use start_capture to begin recording HTTP traffic, get_log to retrieve captured requests with optional filters, and clear to reset.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

action.description: start_capture: enable network capture. stop_capture: disable capture and stop recording. get_log: return captured entries with filters. clear: reset the log.

filter.description: Filters to apply when action is get_log.

url.description: Filter entries by URL substring match.

method.description: Filter by HTTP method (GET, POST, etc).

resourceType.description: Filter by resource type (Document, Stylesheet, Image, Script, XHR, Fetch, etc).

limit.description: Max entries to return (default 50). Only used with get_log.

tools.name: browser_performance
tools.description: Inspect page performance. get_metrics returns Chrome DevTools Performance domain metrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes, etc). get_web_vitals returns Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS) from the page.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

action.description: get_metrics: retrieve CDP Performance.getMetrics data. get_web_vitals: evaluate JS to get Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS).

tools.name: browser_upload
tools.description: Upload files to a <input type='file'> element. Provide the CSS selector for the file input plus `files` (array of absolute paths that must exist on the BROWSER's machine — the machine running Chrome — attached via the Chrome debugger) OR `localFiles` (array of absolute paths on the MCP SERVER machine, streamed to the browser in memory without touching the browser's disk; each file capped at 40 MB by default via transfers.maxFileMb) — provide exactly one of the two. Works for photos, videos, documents — essential for posting to social media (TikTok, Instagram, Twitter).

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

selector.description: CSS selector for the <input type='file'> element

files.description: Array of absolute file paths that must exist on the BROWSER's machine (where Chrome runs) — attached via the Chrome debugger (e.g. ['/home/user/photo.jpg', '/tmp/video.mp4']).

localFiles.description: Array of absolute file paths that must exist on the MCP SERVER machine — the bytes are streamed to the browser in memory (nothing is written to the browser's disk). Each file is size-capped by the transfers.maxFileMb config (default 40 MB).

tools.name: browser_download
tools.description: Download a file from a URL using the browser's built-in download manager. The file is saved on the BROWSER's machine (wherever Chrome runs) under its default downloads folder, optionally in a subdirectory — it does NOT land on the MCP server machine; use browser_fetch_file when you need the bytes on the MCP server. Waits for the download to finish and returns the final absolute filename (Chrome renames on conflicts).

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

url.description: URL to download. If omitted, downloads the current page.

filename.description: Save as filename (e.g. 'photo.jpg'). If omitted, uses the URL filename.

directory.description: Subdirectory under the browser's default downloads folder. If omitted, saves to the default location.

tools.name: browser_clipboard
tools.description: Read, write, or paste clipboard content. Useful for paste-based uploads on social media platforms. 'write' sets clipboard text, 'paste' simulates Ctrl+V into the focused element, 'read' returns current clipboard text.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

action.description: read: read clipboard text content. write: write text to clipboard. paste: simulate Ctrl+V paste into focused element.

text.description: Text to write to clipboard (required for 'write' action)

tools.name: browser_fetch_file
tools.description: Fetch a URL THROUGH the selected browser (its cookies, session, and network position apply) and transfer the bytes to the MCP server machine. The file lands under ~/.mybrowser/transfers/downloads/<sessionId>/ on the MCP server machine together with a .provenance.json sidecar; it is NOT saved in the browser's downloads folder — for browser-local landing use browser_download. inline:true also returns the body as text (up to 256 KB), e.g. for JSON APIs: {url, inline: true}. urls fetches several in one call. Transfers are chunked and sha256-verified; the tool may take up to 5 minutes for larger files. Loopback hostnames are rewritten to the canonical device host when one is configured.

url.description: URL to fetch. The request runs through the selected browser, so its cookies, session, and network position apply. Loopback hostnames are rewritten to the canonical device host when one is configured.

urls.description: Several URLs in one call (up to 50, 2 at a time); one result line per URL. Use instead of one call per file.

filename.description: Filename for the transferred file (sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9._-]). If omitted, uses the last URL path segment. Ignored with urls.

inline.description: Also return the response body as text (JSON, HTML, CSV..., up to 256 KB), so there is no file to read afterwards. Use for API/JSON calls.

tools.name: browser_notes_list
tools.description: List annotated notes the user has saved via the browser extension. Each note is an annotated screenshot plus a text comment. Default returns pending notes only. Use this to see what visual feedback the user has left for you to work through.

status.description: Which notes to list. Default 'pending' — notes the user has saved but not yet been addressed.

tools.name: browser_notes_get
tools.description: Fetch a single note with its full-resolution annotated screenshot. The image includes any arrows, boxes, and text the user drew on the page.

tools.name: browser_notes_archive
tools.description: Mark a note as archived (hidden from the default pending list). Use this after you've addressed the user's feedback so the next agent doesn't see stale items.

resolution.description: Optional short note about how this was resolved (e.g. 'fixed button alignment in Header.tsx'). Preserved on the archived note for audit.

tools.name: browser_notes_unarchive
tools.description: Restore an archived note to pending status so it shows up in the default list again.

id.description: The note ID to restore to pending

tools.name: browser_notes_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a note (both metadata and PNG). Archived notes can be deleted without force; pending notes require force=true to protect unreviewed feedback.

id.description: The note ID to permanently delete

force.description: Required to delete a pending note. Archived notes can always be deleted.

tools.name: browser_on
tools.description: Register an autonomous reaction to a browser event. For example, browser_on('dialog', 'dismiss') auto-closes every alert/confirm/prompt so unattended flows don't stall. Use action='emit' with options.eventName to push events into a named queue you can consume later with browser_wait_for_event. Handlers are session-scoped and cleared on browser disconnect.

event.description: The event to react to. 'dialog' covers alert/confirm/prompt. 'beforeunload' is the unsaved-changes prompt. 'new_tab' fires when the browser opens a popup or target=_blank tab. 'network_timeout' fires when a request stays pending longer than thresholdMs.

action.description: How to react. 'dismiss' closes/cancels. 'accept' confirms (with optional promptText). 'emit' pushes the event to a named queue (set options.eventName) for browser_wait_for_event to consume. For dialogs, 'emit' ALSO implicitly dismisses the dialog so the page can continue — semantics are 'notify AND dismiss'. 'ignore' is a no-op (useful to temporarily disable a broader handler while keeping the registration).

promptText.description: For action=accept on prompt dialogs: the text to submit.

thresholdMs.description: For event=network_timeout: the number of milliseconds a request must remain pending before it's considered stuck. Max 240000 (4 minutes).

eventName.description: For action=emit: the QUEUE NAME to push the event into (this is an arbitrary string you pick; it is NOT the event kind). browser_wait_for_event consumes events from the same queue name, and queues are namespaced per-session so two sessions can reuse names without colliding.

tabId.description: Scope the handler to a specific tab. Omit for browser-wide.

browserId.description: Target browser. Defaults to the active browser for this session.

tools.name: browser_off
tools.description: Unregister an event handler. Pass handlerId to remove a specific one, or omit to remove ALL handlers this session registered (across every browser).

handlerId.description: The specific handler to remove. Omit to remove ALL handlers this session has registered (across every browser, not just the active one).

tools.name: browser_events_list
tools.description: List currently-registered event handlers. Use before browser_off to find handler IDs, or to audit what auto-reactions are active in a session.

browserId.description: Filter to a specific browser. Omit for all browsers.

tools.name: browser_wait_for_event
tools.description: Wait for an event to arrive in a named queue. Pair with browser_on(action='emit', options.eventName='...') to observe events without blocking the whole flow. Returns the event data when one arrives, or {ok:false, reason:'timeout'} after timeoutMs (default 30s).

eventName.description: The queue name to wait on. Must match the eventName in an earlier browser_on(action='emit') call.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait in milliseconds (default 30s). Returns {ok:false, reason:'timeout'} on expiry.

tools.name: browser_lock
tools.description: Acquire a named mutex for coordinating multi-agent critical sections beyond tab ownership. Non-reentrant: a session that already holds the lock cannot re-acquire it (returns error). FIFO fairness: waiters are granted in the order they queued. Optional ttlMs for crash-recovery auto-release. Auto-released when the session disconnects.

name.description: Lock name. Pick a stable identifier for the resource you're guarding (e.g. 'checkout.payment', 'inventory:sku-42'). Up to 128 chars.

timeoutMs.description: Max milliseconds to wait for the lock. Default 30s, max 10 minutes. Returns {acquired:false, reason:'timeout'} if the wait expires.

ttlMs.description: Optional auto-release TTL. If set, the lock releases itself after this many milliseconds even if the owner doesn't call browser_unlock. Max 1 hour. Useful as a crash-recovery safety net.

tools.name: browser_unlock
tools.description: Release a named lock previously acquired with browser_lock. Fails if the caller is not the current owner.

name.description: The lock name to release. Must be the same name passed to browser_lock.

tools.name: browser_locks_list
tools.description: List all currently-held locks. Shows name, owner session id, acquisition time, and TTL expiry (if any).

tools.name: browser_diagnostics
tools.description: Collect MyBrowser MCP diagnostics with redacted sensitive values: server version, connected browsers, sessions, selected browser, recent failures, extension status, and optional recent log tails.

includeLogs.description: Include recent server log tails in the response. Defaults to false.

includeExtension.description: Ask the connected browser extension for its diagnostics. Defaults to true.

tools.name: browser_support_bundle
tools.description: Write a redacted support bundle JSON file under ~/.mybrowser/support-bundles containing diagnostics and recent server log tails.

includeExtension.description: Ask the connected browser extension for its diagnostics. Defaults to true.

tools.name: browser_outline
tools.description: Compact map of every control on the page, including parts below the fold and collapsed sections: grouped by section, each with an id (o12), role, label and current state (on/off, selected option, field value). Use it instead of scrolling and snapshotting to find or check settings. Pass the id as ref: "o12" to browser_click, browser_type, browser_hover or browser_select_option. Ids stay the same across reads of the same page.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

focus.description: What you are looking for, e.g. 'placements and budget'. Returns only the relevant sections.

section.description: Only sections whose title contains this text.

sweep.description: Scroll through the page first so lazily loaded sections are included, then scroll back. Default false.

tools.name: browser_triage
tools.description: Sort a list on the page (invitations, messages, search results, table rows) into your labels, then act on the confirmed cards. Step 1 (dry run, default): reads every card, loading more as needed, and returns each label's cards with ids; with a decision model the labels are assigned for you (unsure ones go to review), without one you get the cards to label yourself. Step 2: call again with action {label, control} and confirm: [ids] to click that control in each confirmed card, paced, re-finding each card before its click, stopping if a dialog opens.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses this session's current tab (opened with new_tab or browser_navigate, or chosen with select_tab), never the user's active tab.

labels.description: Label name -> what it means, e.g. {"ignore": "sells software development or freelance services", "keep": "anyone else"}

cards.description: CSS selector of one card. Default: the page's main repeating list is found automatically.

load.description: Scroll and press 'Show more' until the list stops growing (default true)

minConfidence.description: Labels below this go to review (default 0.8)

labelsById.description: Your own labels for card ids, e.g. from a run without a decision model

control.description: Text of the control inside each card to click, e.g. 'Ignore' or 'Accept'

confirm.description: Card ids to act on, copied from a dry run. Required to click anything.

allowIrreversible.description: Needed when the control deletes, pays, sends, publishes, reports or removes
